Treatment of fresh leachate by microaeration pretreatment combined
with IC-AO2 process: Performance and mechanistic insight
Mengqi Wei a, Ruina Zhang c,d, Mingjian Zhou a, Zhiqiang Yuan a, Haiping Yuan a, Nanwen Zhu a,b,⁎
a School of Environmental Science & Engineering, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Shanghai 200240, China

H I G H L I G H T S
• MAICAO2 process was innovatively

removal efﬁciency than traditional bio-
logical process.

Keywords:
Fresh leachate
Biological treatment
Microaeration
Molecular information
Antibiotics
Fresh leachate is commonly featured with high concentrations of degradable organic matters, which can impede
the performance of traditional biological treatment, especially the anaerobic reactor. Aiming at improving the
biological treatment process of fresh leachate, this study creatively proposed a microaerobic-IC-AO2 (MAICAO2)
process and compared it with traditional biological process, then optimized the operating conditions. Meanwhile,
this work investigated the transformation rules and molecular compositions of dissolved organic matters (DOM)
during MAICAO2 process, particularly the hazardous DOM (antibiotics). The innovative MAICAO2 process can
effectively remove 99% chemical oxygen demand (COD), 91% total nitrogen (TN) and 91% ammonia (NH4
+-N)
during the operation time, and the removal efﬁciencies of COD, TN and NH4
+-N in MAICAO2 process increased
approximately 2%, 14% and 13% compared to ICAOAO process. Electrospray ionization Fourier transform ion
cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry (ESI FT-ICR MS) conﬁrmed that microaeration could ensure over 53%
small molecular organic acids degrade before the subsequent anaerobic reaction so the system could resist the
high concentration organic matters stress and improve the denitriﬁcation efﬁciency. Further analysis showed
that different categories of antibiotics (including 6 sulfonamides, 4 tetracyclines, 2 macrolides, 4 quinolones
and 2 chloramphenicols) could be effectively removed by MAICAO2 process with the total removal efﬁciency
of 50%. This work proposed a new scenario for fresh leachate treatment by proposing the importance of the
microaeration pretreatment during the biological treatment process.

1. Introduction
With the increasing speed of urbanization and the rapid growth of
population, the production of municipal solid waste (MSW) is annually
increasing (Hassan et al., 2016; Song et al., 2020). According to the data
from the National Bureau of Statistic of China, the amount of MSW un-
dergoing innocuous disposal reached 242 million metric tons (t) in
2020 (National Bureau of Statistics of China, 2021). As an effective
method for the reduction of the MSW volume and harvest of the energy,
incineration technology has developed rapidly in recent years (Li et al.,
2017), and the proportion of incineration has reached 50% (National
Bureau of Statistics of China, 2021). In order to ameliorate the corre-
sponding heat value before MSW are incinerated to generate power,
wastes are generally piled up and fermented in a pit for several days
to take moisture away from the wastes (Chen et al., 2020). During this
period, a great amount of fresh leachate could be generated, which ac-
counts for approximately 15%–25% of all MSW (Dang et al., 2016;
Zhou et al., 2017). The resulting leachate contains a complex composi-
tion with a high concentration of organic substances (Liu et al., 2015)
as well as the refractory organics, for example humic and fulvic com-
pounds (Dang et al., 2016). Considering the improper treatment of
fresh leachate will cause irreversible damage to the environment
(Zhang et al., 2019b), it is necessary to explore an effective method for
fresh leachate treatment (Ye et al., 2011).
Currently, leachate are usually treated in biological and physico-
chemical methods (Yuan et al., 2017b). The physicochemical method
can eliminate a large amount of organic matters in fresh leachate. Ad-
vanced oxidation is an effective method for wastewater treatment
(Iovino et al., 2019; Salvestrini et al., 2020). Divyapriya et al. (2021)
discussed the feasibility of photoelectrochemical used to disposal
wastewater. Ozone and Fenton oxidation methods showed high
micro-pollutants degradation potential (Ateş and Argun, 2021). How-
ever, they are expensive and prone to produce secondary pollution
(Miao et al., 2019; Song et al., 2020). In contrast, the biological processes
are extensively used to remove organic and nitrogen from leachate be-
cause of the cost-effectiveness and simplicity (Jokela et al., 2002). Due to
the strict implementation of discharge criteria of leachate (GB 16889-
2008) in China, a combined “anaerobic digestion (AD) + membrane
bioreactor (MBR) + membrane-driven” process is widely used for
leachate treatment (Wang et al., 2020). Nevertheless, in the traditional
biological treatment process, the fast degradation of the organics such
as lipids and proteins in leachate usually lead to the accumulation of
volatile fatty acids (VFAs), therefore reducing the pH drastically
(Carballa et al., 2011; Ding et al., 2021; Yuan et al., 2017a). The decrease
of pH weakened the activity of microorganisms in the anaerobic reactor
(Ding et al., 2021). Furthermore, the massive degradation of organic
matters causes the shortage of carbon sources in the subsequent
denitriﬁcation section (Fu et al., 2015). Although the effect of acidiﬁca-
tion could be offset by enlarging the reactor volume and reducing the in-
ﬂuent load, the degradation of VFAs in AD greatly decreased the ratio of
biochemical oxygen demand to total nitrogen (BOD/TN) of efﬂuent,
resulting in the decline of denitriﬁcation efﬁciency (Begum et al.,
2018). The improvement of traditionally biological treatment process
for fresh leachate is of great signiﬁcance.
Recent studies have demonstrated that the removal efﬁciency of or-
ganic matters could be enhanced by recycling terminal mixture to
microaerobic tank (Benson et al., 2007; Warith, 2002). He et al. (2015)
studied the applying of microaeration, and found that the recirculation
of terminal mixture to the microaerobic tank improved the stability of
the leachate treatment system. The microaerobic tank could not only
buffer the ﬂuctuation of quality and quantity of inﬂuent, but also reduce
the inhibitory impact of acidic pH and high concentrations of ammo-
nium in recycled liquid on microorganisms.
Most of bio-refractory organics in fresh leachate predominantly exist
as dissolved organic matter (DOM), which is a main reason for high
chemical oxygen demand (COD) in efﬂuent (Jiang et al., 2018; Li et al.,
2017). The characteristics of DOM are tightly associated with the treat-
ment and process improvement of leachate disposal. Therefore, the
recognition of the transformation mechanisms of DOM in biological
process is of great signiﬁcance to improve leachate treatment process
(Kunacheva and Stuckey, 2014; Wang and Chen, 2018). However,
most of the analytical methods of the properties of DOM are
ultraviolet-visible spectrometry, gas chromatograph-mass spectrome-
try and three-dimensional ﬂuorescence, which cannot provide accurate
information about transformation rules of DOM (Chen et al., 2019; Ruiz-
Delgado et al., 2020; Xi et al., 2012). Compared with traditional
analytical methods, high resolution mass spectrometry, for example
electrospray ionization Fourier transform ion cyclotron resonance
mass spectrometry (ESI FT-ICR MS), is shown to be a unique method
to provide molecular information of wastewater (Kellerman et al.,
2014; Yuan et al., 2017b; Zhang et al., 2019a). As the dominant sites
for disposal of MSW, incineration plant might receive a variety of
antibiotics from discarded pharmaceuticals, personal care products
and medical wastes (Graham et al., 2011; Threedeach et al., 2012).
Masoner et al. (2014) found that whether in raw or ﬁnal leachate,
antibiotics were generally detectable. Thus, how antibiotics, an impor-
tant type of hazardous DOM, transformed in bio-process of fresh leach-
ate is still unclear.
Therefore, this study innovatively proposed a microaerobic-IC-AO2
process (MAICAO2) in order to improve the pollutant removal efﬁciency
in leachate treatment process, and unravel the decontamination mecha-
nism. Notably, the primary objectives of this study were: (1) to study the
removal efﬁciency of pollutant in MAICAO2 process, and compared it
with traditional biological process, then optimized the operating
conditions including reﬂux ratio (R), reﬂux distribution ratio (RD),
hydraulic retention time (HRT) and sludge retention time (SRT); (2) to
identify the transformation rules and molecular compositions of DOM
in leachate during MAICAO2 process by ESI FT-ICR MS; and (3) to study
the degradation characteristics of selected hazardous DOM, antibiotics.
2. Materials and methods
2.1. Start-up of MAICAO2 system and sample collection
In order to build MAICAO2 system and compare it with traditional
biological treatment, two devices for leachate treatment were designed,
as described in Fig. 1. One of which was a simulated traditional activated
sludge system (ICAOAO, Fig. 1a), and the other was an improved system
(MAICAO2, Fig. 1b). The two devices were wrapped with silicone heat
conductive pad to keep the temperature of the system at 35 °C.
ICAOAO process consisted of two parts, including an IC reactor
(12 L) and an anoxic-oxic-anoxic-oxic tank (8, 8, 8 and 12 L). In
MAICAO2 system, in order to take full use of the high concentration or-
ganic matters in the fresh leachate as the carbon source for denitriﬁca-
tion, the ﬁrst anoxic tank in the traditional process was set before the
anaerobic reactor as a MA tank, and the terminal mixture was recycled
to MA tank. In MA unit (V = 8 L), intermittent aeration was realized by
relay to control dissolved oxygen (DO) < 0.5 mg/L. The working volume
of IC reactor was 12 L. The AO2 tank (28 L) consisted of three consecu-
tive pools, including one denitriﬁcation pool (V = 8 L) and two nitriﬁca-
tion pools (V = 8 and 12 L). The oxic pool was continuously aerated and
the DO was controlled at 3–5 mg/L.
The fresh leachate used in this work was collected from the inciner-
ation plant that stored MSW (2000 t/d) for 5–7 days. The characteristics
of raw leachate were shown in Table 1. In order to maintain the stability
of the system, followed sludge acclimation method was used to culti-
vate the activated sludge for 60 days. The extra sludge produced from
the system was collected for further disposal. Leachate samples were
collected once every two days to evaluate the system performance,
and 3 parallel samples were collected. The ﬁnal value is the average of
the 3 test results. All collected samples were ﬁltered by 0.45 μm mem-
brane at the ﬁrst time, and kept at 4 °C in dark until used.

2.2. Physio-chemical analysis
All reagents that were used in this study were analytical grade. DO
was measured by portable dissolved oxygen meter (HQ40D, HACH
Company, America). pH was measured by pH meter (PHS-25, Shanghai
Leici Company, China). COD, BOD, TN, ammonia (NH4
+-N), nitrate nitro-
gen (NO3
−-N) and suspended solid (SS) were measured in accordance
with the Standard Methods (APHA, 1998). TOC was tested by TOC ana-
lyzer (TOC-V CPH/CPN, Shimadzu Co, Japan).
2.3. Molecular information acquisition by ESI FT-ICR MS and data analysis
In order to remove remaining salts and minimize matrix effects,
solid phase extraction (SPE) process was used to pre-treatment sam-
ples. Leachate samples were collected once every day for 5 days at the
optimal operating conditions, and the samples were mixed for DOM
test. All ﬁltered samples (200 mL) were acidiﬁed with hydrochloric
acid to pH 2 and extracted by SPE. C18 cartridges (500 mg, 6 mL, Waters)
were ﬁrstly activated with acid (pH = 2) and methanol (MS grade);
Leachate samples were added to cartridges at a ﬂow rate of 2 mL/min,
then rinse the cartridges with 20 mL hydrochloric acid (pH = 2) to
eliminate the salts; After that, cartridges were dried with a stream of
N2 and eluted with 1 mL of chromatographic grade methanol and kept
at 4 °C in dark until tested.
A Bruker Apex Ultra ESI FT-ICR MS (Bruker Daltonics, Germany) was
used to analyze samples at the condition of 7 T superconducting mag-
net. All samples were tested in negative ion mode, in which the ion ac-
cumulation, ESI voltages and number of co-added scans were
optimized. A large amount of fragmented molecular ions were gener-
ated at atmospheric pressure coupled with negative ion mode (Fu
et al., 2020; Sleighter et al., 2008). The criteria for eliminating molecular
formula choices was shown below (Koch et al., 2007): (1) double bond
equivalents (DBE) ≥0; (2) the sum of the number of hydrogen and ni-
trogen atoms should be even; (3) the number of carbon atoms must ex-
ceed (H −N −2) / 2 and less than 3 times of the number of hydrogen
atoms; and (4) the number of oxygen or nitrogen atoms should not ex-
ceed the number of carbon atoms.
DBE represents the number of rings and Π bonds in organic matter,
which can be used to explain the degree of saturation of organic matter
in mass spectrometry data. The calculation formula was shown below
(Ohno et al., 2010):
DBE ¼ 1 þ 0:5  2C−H þ n

2.4. Quantiﬁcation of antibiotics
Sample pretreatment and SPE method were used based on the
previous studies (Hou et al., 2015; Luo et al., 2011), as described in the
Text S1. Leachate samples were collected once every two days for 10 days
at the optimal operating conditions and each sample was tested 3 times
in the detection of antibiotics using Ultra High Performance Liquid Chroma-
tography coupled with Triple Quad Mass (UHPLC-3Q-MS, Sciex, Japan). A
total of 18 antibiotics, including 6 sulfonamides (SAs, sulfadiazine, sulfathi-
azole, sulfapyridine, sulfamerazine, sulfamethoxzole, sulfaquinoxaline), 4
tetracyclines (TCs, oxytetracycline, tetracycline, doxycycline, chlortetracy-
cline), 2 macrolides (MLs, erythromycin, roxithromycin), 4 quinolones
(FQs, oﬂoxacin, norﬂoxacin, ciproﬂoxacin, enroﬂoxacin), and 2 chloram-
phenicols (CPs, chloramphenicol, thiamphenicol) were detected. The phys-
icochemical properties of the target antibiotics were presented in Table S1.
Other information of analysis was detailed in the supplemental Text S2 and
Table S2.
3. Results and discussion
3.1. General performance of MAICAO2 process
3.1.1. Comparison of degradation performance on main pollutants between
ICAOAO system and MAICAO2 system
After 60 d-stabilization with the two designed systems at the same
condition (R = 500%, RD = 1:1, HRT = 10 d, SRT = 15 d), the pollutant
removal performance between ICAOAO process and MAICAO2 process
were compared, as shown in Fig. 2. The inﬂuent COD of the two
processes ﬂuctuated slightly, which were 66,281–71,116 mg/L, and
the average COD of inﬂuent was 67,925 mg/L. The average COD of
efﬂuent was 2291 mg/L (ICAOAO process) and 1287 mg/L (MAICAO2
process) respectively. Under the same operating conditions, the
removal rate of COD in MAICAO2 process was increased approximately
2% compared to ICAOAO process, indicating that MAICAO2 system could
decompose organic matters better. This is mainly because the MA tank
could degrade some organic matters and a large amount of small molec-
ular organic acids, then provided a suitable environment for subsequent
reactions. The removal efﬁciency of COD in MA tank reached 83%.
Compared with ICAOAO process, the MA tank reduced the impact load
of the IC reactor, thus making the system more stable. Moreover, IC
digesters have shown better removal efﬁciency of COD (>95%)
compared with other digesters for example anaerobic membrane
bioreactors (Arij et al., 2017; Lim and Kim, 2014; Svojitka et al., 2017).
After MAICAO2 process, the average concentrations of TN, NH4
+-N
and NO3
−-N decreased from 2462, 2358 and 135 mg/L to 322, 242 and
17 mg/L, respectively. While after ICAOAO process, the average concen-
trations of TN, NH4
+-N, and NO3
−-N decreased from 2426, 2295 and
129 mg/L to 521, 473 and 32 mg/L, respectively. The removal efﬁciencies
of TN, NH4
+-N and NO3
−-N in MAICAO2 process were increased approx-
imately 11%, 13% and 16% compared to ICAOAO process. The removal ef-
ﬁciency of TN reached 63% in MA tank. On one hand, the cycled terminal
mixture diluted the organic concentration of the inﬂuent. On the other
hand, simple organics such as small molecule proteins were absorbed
by microorganisms in MA tank, so MA tank exhibited great potential
for pollutant removal. Overall, it could be seen that MAICAO2 process

3.1.2. Optimization of operating conditions of MAICAO2 process
The variations and removal efﬁciencies of COD, TN, NH4
+-N and
NO3
−-N from collected leachate samples of MAICAO2 process were
shown in Fig. 3. From day (d) 100 to day 330, the inﬂuence of R, RD,
HRT and SRT were respectively identiﬁed. The speciﬁc operating
conditions were shown in Table 2. The average concentrations of COD,
TN, NH4
+-N and NO3
−-N in the inﬂuent were 67,768, 2559, 2352 and
129 mg/L during the optimization process. Continuously optimization
obtained the best operating conditions, and improved the removal
performance of the main pollutants in the leachate by biological process.
In phase 1, 3 different gradients of R were controlled, successively
300%, 500%, and 700%. It could be seen from Fig. 3 that the removal efﬁ-
ciency of pollutants was the highest at R of 500%. The average concen-
trations of COD, TN, NH4
+-N and NO3
−-N in the efﬂuent were 1370,
320, 265 and 19 mg/L respectively, with the corresponding removal ef-
ﬁciencies of 98%, 87%, 89% and 85%. It's worth noting that at R of 700%,
the foam in the oxic pool increased, and the activated sludge in the
ﬁrst oxic pool gradually turns black and the settling performance dete-
riorates. The increasing of R would provide more electron acceptors for
the denitriﬁcation section, at the same time bring the DO into the deni-
triﬁcation system, thus destroying the anaerobic environment.
After determining the optimal R as 500%, the inﬂuence of the RD was
explored. The distribution ratios of reﬂux from the ﬁrst oxic pool and
the second oxic pool to MA tank were set as 1:1, 3:2 and 4:1 respec-
tively. As shown in Fig. 3, the removal efﬁciency was highest at RD of
3:2. The average concentrations of COD, TN, NH4
+-N and NO3
−-N de-
creased from 67,025, 2426, 2352 and 124 mg/L to 1287, 264, 252 and
24 mg/L, and the removal efﬁciencies were 98%, 89%, 89% and 81% re-
spectively. There was a signiﬁcant difference in the removal efﬁciency
under different RD, because the diverse RD would lead to different C/N
ratio in denitriﬁcation section, resulting in great difference in nitrogen
removal efﬁciency.
The HRT was a vital factor in the wastewater treatment process
(Lusinier et al., 2020), and it was controlled by inﬂuent ﬂow rate. There-
fore, the effect of HRT (8, 10 and 12 d) on the process was explored dur-
ing phase 3. Compared with the other two conditions, the pollutant
removal efﬁciency was the highest at HRT of 12 d. The average

concentrations of COD, TN, NH4

because of insufﬁcient matrix content, which would decompose part
of the intracellular or extracellular organic matter, and the removal
rate would no longer increase but decrease (Fall et al., 2014).
In phase 4, the inﬂuence of SRT on the system was explored, succes-
sively 10, 15 and 20 d. The number of microorganisms was greatly de-
creased at SRT of 10 d, while the settling performance of activated
sludge was observed to deteriorate at SRT of 20 d. Under normal condi-
tion, the concentration of SS in aerobic tank was maintained at
4000–6000 mg/L. However, the concentration of SS was tested as
5500–7000 mg/L at SRT of 20 d. The poor settling performance most
likely resulted from high SS. The removal rate of pollutants reached
the highest at SRT of 15 d. The average concentrations of COD, TN,
NH4
+-N and NO3
−-N in the efﬂuent were 995, 229, 227 and 22 mg/L,
with the corresponding removal rate of 99%, 91%, 91% and 83%. Song
et al. (2020) studied the removal performance of pollutants by anoxic
rotating biological contactor and four oxic tanks, and the removal efﬁ-
ciencies were 86%, 84% and 99% for COD, TN and NH4
+-N. We conducted
a multi-factor analysis of variance for the four parameters (R, RD, HRT
and SRT), as shown in Table S3. The p values of the four parameters
for COD, TN and NH4
+-N were all less than 0.05, indicating that the
four parameters have a signiﬁcant impact on COD, TN and NH4
+-N of
the efﬂuent. The p value of RD for NO3
−-N was less than 0.05 while the
p values of R, HRT and SRT for NO3
−-N were higher than 0.05. This sug-
gested that signiﬁcant impact exist between RD and NO3
−-N, and R,
HRT and SRT have no obvious effect on NO3
−-N.
From the above analysis, the optimal operating conditions were as
follows: R = 500%, RD = 2:3, HRT = 12 d and SRT = 15 d. After 330
d-treatment by the improved process, we reached relatively high re-
moval efﬁciencies of COD > 99%, TN > 91%, NH4
+-N > 91% in MAICAO2
process, and the removal efﬁciencies were increased approximately
2%, 14% and 13% compared to ICAOAO process.
3.2. DOM transformation analysis by ESI FT-ICR MS
3.2.1. Molecular weight transformation of DOM
DOM is an important part of COD, whether COD can be further re-
moved by improving the bio-process generally depends on the molecu-
lar weight and composition of DOM. Therefore, it is necessary to analyze
the transformation mechanisms of DOM in biological treatment pro-
cesses. Analyses and statistics of ESI FT-ICR MS data were used to recog-
nize the molecular information of DOM in fresh leachate, including
molecular weight distribution diagram, van Krevelen diagram and
DBE diagram (Nguyen et al., 2012). The whole mass value was set at
m/z 100–1000, while the sample mass spectra mainly focused on
100–500 m/z (Fig. S1). It could be demonstrated from the original
mass spectra that the distribution of masses in MA efﬂuent was more
regular than that in raw leachate and the mass distribution towards
higher. The normal distribution of DOM was obviously observed after
the anaerobic reaction, illustrating that the types of organic matter
increased. During the anaerobic process, microorganisms used the
original organic matter as a carbon source to metabolize and produce
bio-derived organic matter. ESI FT-ICR MS demonstrated the molecular
weight distribution of leachate samples among fresh leachate, MA efﬂu-
ent, IC efﬂuent and AO2 efﬂuent (Fig. 4). Percentage of m/z 100–400 de-
creased from 57% (raw leachate) to 27% (MA efﬂuent), and about 53%
small molecular organic acids degrade before the anaerobic reaction.
As the process progressed, the distribution of DOM became increasingly
normal, indicated that complex organics were gradually degraded into
simple compounds. In the MA tank, the proportion of small molecule or-
ganics (especially small molecule organic acids) decreased, making
small molecule organics truly participate in denitriﬁcation as carbon
source. Meanwhile, small molecule organics were not accumulated in
MA tank due to microaeration environment, which provided the suit-
able concentration of small molecule organics for continuous reaction.
3.2.2. Molecular composition transformation of DOM
van Krevelen diagram analysis is a crucial method to illustrate accu-
rate molecular formulae. The diagram is element-ratio plots, and each
dot in the diagram represents the molar ratio of oxygen to carbon (O/C)
on the x-axis and molar ratio of hydrogen to carbon (H/C) on the y-axis
for that speciﬁc formula. Based on O/C and H/C ratio, leachate DOM has
been divided into 9 categories corresponding to 9 groups in van Krevelen
diagram (Fig. 5). In order to acquire more information, DOM in leachate
were categorized into 4 groups after further calculations (Nuerenberg
et al., 2019), namely aliphatic compounds (CHO), phenolic compounds
(CHON), polyphenols (CHOS) and polycyclic aromatics (CHONS). The
major components in leachate were composed of these 4 groups of
DOM with speciﬁc element ratio (Fu et al., 2020).
A total of 4098, 6049, 6481 and 7488 molecule formulas of DOM
were detected after select among raw leachate, MA efﬂuent, IC efﬂuent
and AO2 efﬂuent, respectively (Fig. 5a–d). It was worth noting that the
numbers and types of DOM in the leachate increased along the process,
which indicated that a great amount of bio-derived DOM were pro-
duced during biological process (Patriarca et al., 2018), and the number
of components showed obvious difference. The majority of compounds
in raw leachate were lipid-like (35%, group I), protein/peptides-like
(22%, group II), and CRAM or lignin-like (35%, group VII). Considering
raw leachate was initial product of hydrolytic acidiﬁcation of MSW
(Eggen et al., 2010; Kjeldsen et al., 2002), the transformation of multiple
DOM was normal phenomenon. The proportion of lipid-like decreased
from 35% (raw leachate) to 6% (AO2 efﬂuent), illustrating that microor-
ganisms degraded large number of lipid-like compounds with high H/C
and O/C ratio in biological treatment and Lipid-like compounds were
highly biodegradable. In contrast, CRAM or lignin-like compounds in-
creased from 35% (raw leachate) to 64% (AO2 efﬂuent), which suggested
CRAM or lignin-like were bio-derived compounds. Compared with raw
leachate, the composition of organic compounds in ﬁnal efﬂuent
changed a lot, and the total content was higher and the relative intensity
was strikingly increased. In MAICAO2 system, some native DOM were
degraded and a large amount of bio-derived DOM were produced.
Fig. 5 showed that DOM in the efﬂuent of different units had obvi-
ously complex composition and composed of numerous organics after
selected, and these compounds were concentrated in the 4 groups
(CHO, CHON, CHOS, CHONS). After the treatment of biological process,
bioavailable DOM (for example CHO) was substantially eliminated,
and the relative abundance of other three classes increased dramati-
cally. A large amount of CHON were produced in anaerobic process

3.3. Occurrence and distribution of selected hazardous DOM: antibiotics
Antibiotic, as a kind of hazardous DOM, has been regarded as envi-
ronmental contaminants owing to associated risks exhibit to human,
and it can get into the environment through incineration plant. There-
fore, the concentration variation of antibiotics during biological treat-
ment process was detected in this work. The average concentrations
of all tested antibiotics and the concentrations of speciﬁc antibiotic in
leachate sample were displayed in Fig. 7. A total of 18 antibiotics, includ-
ing 6 sulfonamides (SQ, SMT, SM, SP, STZ and SDZ), 4 tetracyclines (CTC,
DOC, TC and OTC), 2 macrolides (RTM and ETM), 4 quinolones (EFX,
CFX, NFX and OFX), and 2 chloramphenicols (TAP and CAP) were
detected in raw leachate. After MAICAO2 process, the average concen-
tration of 18 antibiotics decreased from 10.5 ± 0.8 to 5.1 ± 0.9 μg/L.
All antibiotics could still be detected in the efﬂuent, meaning that this

process could not completely remove antibiotics. The average removal
rate of all antibiotics was about 50%, indicating the feasibility of this
improved system for treating fresh leachate (Li et al., 2013).
Most detected antibiotics in raw leachate (TAP, CAP, RTM, ETM, SQ,
SMT, SM, SP, STZ, SDZ, CFX, NFX, CTC, TC, OTC) were in the ng/L level,
and relatively higher concentrations (μg/L level) were tested for EFX
(1.8 ± 0.5 μg/L), OFX (3.6 ± 0.8 μg/L) and DOC (1.7 ± 0.6 μg/L). The
dominant antibiotics in raw leachate were EFX, OFX and DOC, which ac-
count for about 67% of the total detected antibiotics. FQs and TCs were 2
dominant types of antibiotics in the inﬂuent with the average concen-
trations of 5.5 and 3.2 μg/L respectively, while the average concentra-
tions of most subtypes of CPs, MLs and SAs were no more than 0.5 μg/L.
The analysis based on type suggested that the removal efﬁciencies of
TCs and SAs were about 71% and 64%, and AO2 reactors showed better
removal performance compared to IC reactor (9% and 34%, respec-
tively). The removal rate of TCs was the highest, and we speculate that
the decrease of TCs was related to bio-sorption of activated sludge.
The adsorption of TCs was usually a chemical process and dominated
by ionic interaction, hydrophobicity, hydrogen bonding and cation
bonding (Liao et al., 2021). The biodegradation of antibiotics was af-
fected by the content of available DO, it is logical for IC reactor showed
lower removal efﬁciency of antibiotics (Lin and Gan, 2011). Kang et al.
(2018) studied the removal of SMX in anoxic-anaerobic-oxic system,
and found that aerobic biodegradation was the major removal pathway
while sorption and anoxic-anaerobic system were insigniﬁcant. Zhao
et al. (2018) investigated the removal efﬁciency of nine SAs by
anaerobic-anoxic-oxic-membrane system, and conﬁrmed that aerobic
biodegradation made the largest contribution to the removal of antibi-
otics. In our study, anaerobic reactor showed lower removal efﬁciency
of 18 antibiotics compared to AO2, and the conclusion were consistent
with the results discussed above. Under aerobic condition, activated
sludge was found capable of utilizing antibiotics as carbon source, and
the adsorption performance of sludge was better compared to anaerobic
condition. On the contrary, MLs, FQs and CPs were removed with lower
efﬁciencies (41%, 42% and 38%, respectively). Overall, MAICAO2 system
exhibits great potential for the antibiotics removal, and the antibiotics
were better removed by AO2 reactor compared to IC reactor.
4. Conclusion
In this study, MAICAO2 process was proven to be more efﬁcient to si-
multaneously remove organic matters and nitrogen compared to
ICAOAO process. MAICAO2 system steadily performed for 330 d, and
the average concentrations of COD, TN and NH4
+-N decreased from
67,768, 2563 and 2433 mg/L to 995, 229 and 227 mg/L. The removal ef-
ﬁciencies of COD, TN and NH4
+-N in MAICAO2 process increased approx-
imately 2%, 14% and 13% compared to ICAOAO process, respectively.
Efﬂuent recirculation, HRT and SRT showed to be important parameters
to improve removal efﬁciencies, and the optimal operating conditions
were: R = 500%, RD = 3:2, HRT = 12 d and SRT = 15 d.
High resolution mass spectrometry analysis indicated microaeration
ensured more than 53% of small molecular organic acids degraded be-
fore the anaerobic reaction. About 3390 kinds of bio-derived DOM
were produced during the process of biological treatment. Antibiotics,
as a kind of hazardous DOM, could be effectively removed by MAICAO2
process with the average removal rate of 50%. TCs and SAs were
removed with high efﬁciencies (71% and 64%), while MLs, FQs, and
CPs were worse removed (41%, 42% and 38% respectively). This
study could provide a feasible idea for the improvement of fresh leach-
ate treatment especially about the application of microaeration
pretreatment.
